meta.what: Every factor of the project with its status, and the new per-place factors for the page.

statuses.measured and used in the ranking: Measured, or calculated from measured data, and part of the score that puts the lists in order.
statuses.measured and shown: Read from a measured map, a catalogue or a model grid, and shown for each place. It is not part of the score.
statuses.rough estimate by our own rule: A word that our own stated rule sets from other layers. It is not a measurement.
statuses.planet side only: We have figures for the lunar regions or the Mars sites, but not for the places on Earth.
statuses.being built: Another member of the team did not complete the input file yet.
statuses.not built: There is no figure. The table gives the reason.

kinds.measured: measured from a map, a catalogue or the calculated path of the Sun, for the area itself
kinds.model: a model value (reanalysis or climate model) at the nearest grid point
kinds.coarse map: a value of a grid box that is much larger than the area, not a measurement at the place
kinds.rough estimate by our rule: a word that our own stated rule sets, not a measurement

meta.status_rule: Read from the files: a factor with known values for Earth places is measured (in the ranking or shown) or a rough estimate by its kind; with figures only for the lunar regions or Mars sites it is 'planet side only'; otherwise 'not built' with the reason, or 'being built' when another member's file is still missing.
meta.left_out: The table has no row for pits, caves and skylights, because the team lead removed them.
meta.caption: Drawn by code from open data; the code was written with AI assistance.
meta.nav_sentence: These figures are parts of the problem of navigation by sight. We do not give one score for them.
meta.coarse_warning: A value from a coarse grid is the value of a box that is much larger than the area. It is not a measurement at the place.
meta.card_lead: New factors for this area. Each figure has a tag for its kind. If we have a figure for the lunar region, the card shows it also.
meta.south_permafrost_note: The literature says that all ice-free ground in Antarctica is permafrost. The permafrost map does not include Antarctica.
meta.tremor_blind_spots: This is a count of catalogued events, not a measurement of ground motion at the place, and not a hazard map. Only a seismometer at the place gives a real test. The networks of seismometers increased during the 16 years. In some places, for example the Kobuk valley, the later years have several times as many events a year as the early years. Thus, the early years show too few events, and the number of years with events can be too low. Distances are from the centre of the place.
meta.tremor_cannot_tell: Cannot tell: the catalogue does not record small tremors here. Thus, an empty circle around the place does not show that there are no small tremors.
meta.existing_rows_note: This part does not repeat the factors that are on the place card already.

matrix.name: Sun height and low-Sun hours
matrix.what_it_is: The hours in a year when the centre of the Sun is above the horizon but below the Sun ceiling of the lunar region. Only spells of 2 h or more count.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not the sunshine below cloud, and it is not the height of the Sun at one moment.
matrix.earth_figure_from: We calculated the path of the Sun at each minute for each area, first over a flat horizon, then over the real hills.
matrix.moon_figure_from: We calculated the Sun ceiling of each lunar region from its latitude and the 1.54 degree tilt of the Moon.
matrix.mars_figure_from: The Mars part does not use it. That part compares climate and ground, not low Sun.
matrix.status: measured and used in the ranking

matrix.name: Cloud
matrix.what_it_is: The mean cloud amount for each month in the 1 degree box that holds the area. Step 4 keeps the hours that remain under typical cloud.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not the cloud during the hours of low Sun, and it is not a measurement at the area.
matrix.earth_figure_from: NASA POWER climatology, CERES SYN1deg cloud amount.
matrix.moon_figure_from: The Moon has no air and no cloud.
matrix.mars_figure_from: The Mars part does not use it.
matrix.status_reason: Step 4 of the map removes the hours that typical cloud hides. The scores that put the lists in order do not use it.

matrix.name: UV exposure
matrix.what_it_is: The mean UV index at the ground for each month, below the real sky, over all 24 hours of the day.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not the noon UV index of a weather forecast, and it is not a measurement at the place.
matrix.earth_figure_from: NASA POWER climatology ALLSKY_SFC_UV_INDEX, CERES SYN1deg 1 degree box.
matrix.moon_figure_from: The Moon has no air or ozone to filter UV. Our data has no UV figure for the Moon.
matrix.mars_figure_from: Our data has no UV figure for Mars.

matrix.name: Surface sunlight
matrix.what_it_is: The sunlight that gets to level ground in a mean day of each month, below the real mix of cloud and clear sky. The night is included.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not the light on a tilted panel, and it is not a measurement at the place.
matrix.earth_figure_from: NASA POWER climatology ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN, CERES SYN1deg.
matrix.moon_figure_from: The share of all time that the lunar regions are in sunlight, from the PGDA illumination maps. Our data does not have the energy for each day.
matrix.mars_figure_from: The NASA fact sheet gives the sunlight at the top of the Mars atmosphere.

matrix.name: Clear-sky days
matrix.what_it_is: The days in a typical year (2001 to 2020) when the daytime cloud in the 1 degree box is less than 10 percent.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not the days of clear sky during the hours of low Sun, and it is not a count at the place.
matrix.earth_figure_from: NASA POWER climatology CLRSKY_DAYS, divided by its 20 years.
matrix.moon_figure_from: Each day is clear on the Moon, because there is no air.
matrix.mars_figure_from: Our data has no figure for Mars.

matrix.name: Dust and haze
matrix.what_it_is: How much the dust, smoke and haze in the air decrease the light of the Sun. The figure is the aerosol optical depth of the 1 degree box.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not the dust on the ground. It is not dust only, but all aerosol together.
matrix.earth_figure_from: NASA POWER climatology AOD_55_ADJ for the areas and AOD_55 for the Mars squares. The service has no figure for dust only.
matrix.moon_figure_from: The Moon has no air, thus it has no haze. Lunar dust is on the ground.
matrix.mars_figure_from: Martinez et al. 2017 describe the dusty sky of Mars in words only.

matrix.name: Hills around the area
matrix.what_it_is: The real horizon of each area, from a 60 m height model. It removes the hours of low Sun that the hills hide.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not the shade from plants or buildings.
matrix.earth_figure_from: Copernicus DEM GLO-90 horizons, step 3 of the map.
matrix.moon_figure_from: The 5 m LOLA models of the lunar regions (PGDA product 78).
matrix.mars_figure_from: The Mars part does not use it.
matrix.status: measured and used in the ranking

matrix.name: Slope
matrix.what_it_is: The median and 90th-percentile slope of the ground in a 10 km window, from a 90 m height model.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not the slope below one footprint. The 90 m pixels remove small steps in the ground.
matrix.earth_figure_from: Copernicus DEM GLO-90. For the Mars squares: slopes across approximately 3.7 km.
matrix.moon_figure_from: LOLA 5 m models, slopes on 90 m blocks.
matrix.mars_figure_from: MOLA heights every 1.85 km at the Mars sites.

matrix.name: Slope likeness
matrix.what_it_is: How much the distribution of slopes in the area overlaps the distribution of slopes in the lunar region.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It does not compare single landforms, and it cannot see features smaller than 90 m.
matrix.earth_figure_from: Copernicus DEM GLO-90 slopes.
matrix.moon_figure_from: LOLA 5 m models on 90 m blocks.
matrix.mars_figure_from: MOLA slopes across approximately 3.7 km.
matrix.status: measured and used in the ranking

matrix.name: Roughness at several scales
matrix.what_it_is: How rough the ground is after we remove the local slope, at baselines of 90, 270 and 810 m.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It does not show boulders, because on Earth the model cannot see features smaller than 90 m. GLO-90 includes forest and buildings.
matrix.earth_figure_from: Copernicus DEM GLO-90 in a 10 km window.
matrix.moon_figure_from: LOLA 5 m models at 5, 15, 45, 90, 270 and 810 m.
matrix.mars_figure_from: We did not calculate it for the Mars squares, because their heights are 1.85 km apart.

matrix.name: Landforms
matrix.what_it_is: Plain, rolling ground, hills or mountains. Limits on slope and relief set the class, after Hammond (1964).
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not a geomorphological map. Nobody checked it in the field.
matrix.earth_figure_from: A Copernicus DEM GLO-90 window. For the Mars squares: a relief class only.
matrix.moon_figure_from: The same rule, used on 10 km pieces of the 5 m LOLA models.
matrix.mars_figure_from: A relief class at the Mars sites.
matrix.status: rough estimate by our own rule

matrix.name: Visual navigation difficulty
matrix.what_it_is: The page shows its four parts next to each other. The parts are the height of the Sun, the share of ground in terrain shadow, the roughness at 90 m and the haze.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not one score. We do not give a score.
matrix.earth_figure_from: The sources of each part (Sun path, horizons, GLO-90, NASA POWER aerosol).
matrix.moon_figure_from: The Sun ceiling, the lit share and the roughness of the lunar regions.
matrix.mars_figure_from: We did not make it for the Mars part.

matrix.name: Bare ground
matrix.what_it_is: The share of the land in the area that is bare rock, gravel or sand, without plants or permanent ice.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It does not mean that the ground is free of snow in each season. Snow is a separate step.
matrix.earth_figure_from: ESA WorldCover 10 m 2021 (north) and the SCAR rock outcrop layer (south).
matrix.moon_figure_from: The lunar regions are bare regolith.
matrix.mars_figure_from: ESA WorldCover 2021 for the Mars squares.
matrix.status: measured and used in the ranking

matrix.name: Snow
matrix.what_it_is: The odds that the area is free of snow in each ten-day period, from daily snow maps of past years.
matrix.what_it_is_not: Snow is not measured in the south. There, the page uses the rock season.
matrix.earth_figure_from: NOAA / U.S. National Ice Center IMS snow maps through NSIDC.
matrix.moon_figure_from: The Moon has no snow.
matrix.mars_figure_from: The Mars part does not use it. It uses temperature and dryness.
matrix.status: measured and used in the ranking

matrix.name: Anorthosite
matrix.what_it_is: This tells if the area is on a listed body of anorthosite, the rock of the bright highlands of the Moon.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not a rock map of the area. Each listed body is a circle around its published centre.
matrix.earth_figure_from: Our list of anorthosite bodies from the literature.
matrix.moon_figure_from: The lunar regions are highland anorthosite.
matrix.mars_figure_from: The Mars squares that are on a listed body.
matrix.status: measured and used in the ranking

matrix.name: Albedo (surface brightness)
matrix.what_it_is: The share of sunlight that the ground reflects, as a mean of the sunlit months of the year, for a 1 degree box.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not the brightness of bare rock, because the box contains a mix of snow, sea and plants.
matrix.earth_figure_from: NASA POWER ALLSKY_SRF_ALB, CERES SYN1deg.
matrix.moon_figure_from: We did not read a file of lunar albedo for this version of the page.
matrix.mars_figure_from: MGS TES albedo mosaic at each Mars site.

matrix.name: Volcanic and basaltic material
matrix.what_it_is: This tells if the main rock of the half-degree box is volcanic, and if it is like basalt (basic volcanic).
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not the rock at the place. It is only the main rock of a box of approximately 55 km.
matrix.earth_figure_from: GLiM rock map, Hartmann and Moosdorf 2012, half-degree grid.
matrix.moon_figure_from: The lunar regions are highland anorthosite, not mare basalt.
matrix.mars_figure_from: Our data has no rock class for each Mars site.

matrix.name: Mineralogy
matrix.what_it_is: The usual minerals of the mapped rock class of the area, from one table that we made. The table also tells how much they are like the Moon and Mars.
matrix.what_it_is_not: We read it from a rock map, not from spectra.
matrix.earth_figure_from: GLiM rock class and our anorthosite list.
matrix.moon_figure_from: Highland anorthosite (plagioclase-rich) at the lunar regions.
matrix.mars_figure_from: Our data has no mineral figure for each Mars site.
matrix.status: rough estimate by our own rule

matrix.name: Silicate composition
matrix.what_it_is: Which silicate minerals are the main ones (plagioclase, pyroxene and olivine, quartz). We read them from the mineral family.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not a chemical analysis. We did not read a figure for an element or an oxide.
matrix.earth_figure_from: We use the row for the mineral family in its place.
matrix.moon_figure_from: Plagioclase-rich highland rock.
matrix.mars_figure_from: Our data has no figure for each Mars site.
matrix.status: rough estimate by our own rule

matrix.name: Spectral match
matrix.what_it_is: How closely the spectrum that the ground reflects matches the spectra of the Moon or Mars.
matrix.what_it_is_not: The mineral family is not a spectral match.
matrix.earth_figure_from: We did not make this figure.
matrix.moon_figure_from: We did not make this figure.
matrix.mars_figure_from: We did not make this figure.
matrix.status_reason: We did not read spectra of places on Earth or of the lunar regions for this version of the page. We use the row for the mineral family in its place.

matrix.name: Thermal inertia
matrix.unit: class; index in 1 per degree C
matrix.what_it_is: How fast the ground heats and cools. Our index is (1 - albedo) divided by the daily swing of air temperature. We divide the places into thirds by this index.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not thermal inertia. It is an index from coarse climate grids.
matrix.earth_figure_from: NASA POWER albedo and temperature swing.
matrix.moon_figure_from: There is no Diviner product for thermal inertia at the poles.
matrix.mars_figure_from: TES night thermal inertia map at the Mars sites.
matrix.status: rough estimate by our own rule

matrix.name: Resource-use materials
matrix.what_it_is: This tells if rock with ilmenite (the oxygen ore in lunar plans) is possible, from the mapped rock class.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not an ore survey. It gives no assay and no grade.
matrix.earth_figure_from: GLiM rock class and our anorthosite list.
matrix.moon_figure_from: Lunar Prospector hydrogen at the lunar regions is the main resource figure.
matrix.mars_figure_from: Odyssey GRS water at the Mars sites.
matrix.status: rough estimate by our own rule

matrix.name: Rock abundance
matrix.what_it_is: Rockiness: a word that we set from the bare share, steep or rough ground and loose sediment. We use it in place of rock abundance.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not a count of rocks or boulders. Heights at intervals of 90 m cannot show single rocks.
matrix.earth_figure_from: The bare-ground share, the terrain and ground figures and the GLiM rock map.
matrix.moon_figure_from: The Diviner rock map stops at 80 S. All the lunar regions are farther south.
matrix.mars_figure_from: We did not find a file of numbers for rock abundance on Mars.
matrix.status: rough estimate by our own rule

matrix.name: Surface activity
matrix.what_it_is: Ground that changes by itself today, for example dunes that move, streaks on slopes and frost.
matrix.what_it_is_not: The rate at Gale is the rate of the dune field, not of the landing point.
matrix.earth_figure_from: There is no figure for each area.
matrix.moon_figure_from: We expect none (NASA 2024 release).
matrix.mars_figure_from: At Gale, the dunes move approximately 1 m a year (NASA APOD).
matrix.status_reason: There is no figure for each place on Earth. There are figures for the lunar regions or the Mars sites.

matrix.name: Temperature
matrix.what_it_is: The mean air temperature 2 m above the ground for each month, at the nearest grid point.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not the temperature of the ground surface, and it is not a measurement at the place.
matrix.earth_figure_from: NASA POWER climatology T2M, MERRA-2.
matrix.moon_figure_from: Diviner model temperatures at the lunar regions.
matrix.mars_figure_from: Mars Climate Database at the Mars sites.

matrix.name: Daily temperature swing
matrix.what_it_is: The temperature of the warmest hour of the day minus the temperature of the coldest hour, for air 2 m above the ground. It is a mean for each month.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not the swing at the ground surface, and it is not a measurement at the place.
matrix.earth_figure_from: NASA POWER T2M_RANGE, MERRA-2.
matrix.moon_figure_from: The Diviner polar tables were too large to read for this version of the page.
matrix.mars_figure_from: Mars Climate Database ground and air swing.

matrix.name: Wind
matrix.what_it_is: The mean wind speed 10 m above the ground for all hours, at the nearest grid point.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It does not show gusts, or valley winds that are smaller than the grid box.
matrix.earth_figure_from: NASA POWER WS10M, MERRA-2.
matrix.moon_figure_from: The Moon has no air and no wind.
matrix.mars_figure_from: Our data has no wind figure for Mars.

matrix.name: Soil moisture
matrix.what_it_is: The wetness of the top 5 cm of soil, from 0 (dry) to 1 (saturated), from a land model.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not a measurement with a probe. If the value is 1 all year, the grid point of the model is ice.
matrix.earth_figure_from: NASA POWER GWETTOP, MERRA-2.
matrix.moon_figure_from: Lunar soil contains no liquid water.
matrix.mars_figure_from: There is no liquid water at the surface. See near-surface water.

matrix.name: Permafrost
matrix.what_it_is: The probability of permafrost from a model, as a mean of the 1 km pixels in the area, and the permafrost zone.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not a measurement in the ground. This map does not include Antarctica.
matrix.earth_figure_from: Obu et al. 2019 Northern Hemisphere permafrost map, 1 km.
matrix.moon_figure_from: The polar ground of the Moon is frozen all year. See depth to stable ice.
matrix.mars_figure_from: The depth of ice at the Mars sites. See depth to stable ice.

matrix.name: Depth to stable ice
matrix.what_it_is: The depth at which frozen ground or stable ice starts. On Earth, our rule sets a class from the permafrost zone.
matrix.what_it_is_not: On Earth, it is not a measurement of the depth of thaw.
matrix.earth_figure_from: Our rule, used on the permafrost zone. We did not find depths in metres.
matrix.moon_figure_from: Diviner model depth to stable ice.
matrix.mars_figure_from: Phoenix: 3 to 5 cm, from the trench that the lander dug. Arcadia and Deuteronilus: published words.
matrix.status: rough estimate by our own rule

matrix.name: Near-surface hydrogen or water
matrix.what_it_is: On Earth, our rule sets classes for water in the top soil and for ground ice. On the Moon and Mars, instruments in orbit measure hydrogen.
matrix.what_it_is_not: On Earth, it is not a measurement of hydrogen from orbit. The figures for the Moon and Mars are for a region, not for the landing point.
matrix.earth_figure_from: NASA POWER top-soil wetness and the permafrost map.
matrix.moon_figure_from: Lunar Prospector neutron spectrometer, half-degree bins.
matrix.mars_figure_from: Mars Odyssey GRS, 5 degree bins.
matrix.status: rough estimate by our own rule

matrix.name: Large earthquakes
matrix.what_it_is: The catalogued earthquakes of magnitude 5 or more within 200 km from 1990 to 2025, with the largest one and the nearest one.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not a hazard map, and it is not a forecast.
matrix.earth_figure_from: USGS ANSS ComCat.
matrix.moon_figure_from: A NASA release from 2024 about moonquakes near the south pole, in words only.
matrix.mars_figure_from: The 1,319 marsquakes that InSight recorded for the whole planet.

matrix.name: Steady small tremors
matrix.what_it_is: The catalogued events of magnitude 1 to less than 5 within 100 km, from 2010 to 2025. It also tells if the catalogue can see them here.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not the ground motion at the place. If the network has few stations, the answer is 'cannot tell'.
matrix.earth_figure_from: USGS ANSS ComCat small events.
matrix.moon_figure_from: No seismometer worked near the south pole at any time.
matrix.mars_figure_from: InSight, for the whole planet only.

matrix.name: Active volcanism
matrix.what_it_is: Our class from the volcanoes within 30 or 100 km that erupted in 1990 or later, and the nearest Holocene volcano.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not a hazard map, and it is not a forecast of eruptions.
matrix.earth_figure_from: Smithsonian GVP Holocene volcano list.
matrix.moon_figure_from: The Moon has no active volcanism.
matrix.mars_figure_from: We know of no active volcanism on Mars today.
matrix.status: rough estimate by our own rule

matrix.name: Airfield distance
matrix.what_it_is: The straight-line distance to the nearest airfield, and to the nearest airfield with scheduled flights.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is a straight-line distance, not a travel time.
matrix.earth_figure_from: OurAirports, public domain.
matrix.moon_figure_from: Not applicable.
matrix.mars_figure_from: Airfields near the Mars squares.

matrix.name: Human footprint
matrix.what_it_is: Our class from the settlements, main roads and airfields near the area, and the people in listed settlements within 100 km.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not a population map. The lists do not include stations or settlements of less than 1,000 people.
matrix.earth_figure_from: GeoNames cities1000, Natural Earth roads, OurAirports.
matrix.moon_figure_from: There are no people.
matrix.mars_figure_from: There are no people.
matrix.status: rough estimate by our own rule

matrix.name: Remoteness
matrix.what_it_is: The straight-line distance to the nearest listed settlement and to the nearest city of 50,000 people or more.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not a travel time. The words 'no settlement within 100 km' do not mean that nobody lives there.
matrix.earth_figure_from: GeoNames cities1000, CC BY 4.0.
matrix.moon_figure_from: Not applicable.
matrix.mars_figure_from: Not applicable.

matrix.name: Power from sun, wind and ground heat
matrix.what_it_is: Our classes for solar panels, for wind at 50 m and for geothermal plants near the area.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It does not give the power output of a real system.
matrix.earth_figure_from: NASA POWER and the geothermal plant list.
matrix.moon_figure_from: The lit share of the lunar region.
matrix.mars_figure_from: The sunlight on Mars, from the fact sheet.
matrix.status: rough estimate by our own rule

matrix.name: Land status and permits
matrix.what_it_is: Who owns or governs the ground at the centre of the area, and if a protected area is there. It also tells whom to ask for a permit. Some classes come from open maps, and the other classes come from territory rules.
matrix.what_it_is_not: It is not legal advice. We test only the centre of the area. A territory rule is a rough guide, not a land survey. Each map covers only its own region.
matrix.earth_figure_from: Natural Earth boundaries give the territory, and official pages give each territory rule. If a polygon on an open map of protected areas or owners contains the centre, that map sets the class.
matrix.moon_figure_from: Not applicable. Our data has no land status for the Moon.
matrix.mars_figure_from: The same territory rules and maps, used for the Mars squares on Earth where a map covers the square.
matrix.status: rough estimate by our own rule

fields.label: What the territory rule says about owners
codes: unknown: we did not read an official page about who owns the land.
Under the Land Code of the Russian Federation, land can be private, municipal or state property. All land that citizens, legal entities or municipalities do not own is state property.

Alaska is a mix of federal land, State of Alaska land, Alaska Native Corporation land and other private land. In 1959, when Alaska became a state, almost all of its land was federal. The BLM surveys land and transfers it to individual Alaska Natives, Alaska Native corporations and the State of Alaska.
Land in Nunavut is Crown land, Commissioner's land or Inuit Owned Land. Some privately owned land is also inside municipal boundaries.

Greenland has joint ownership of land. Thus, nobody can buy or sell land. A person or a company gets a right of use through an area allotment. The official page says joint ownership, not public land. Here, our class 'public land' means this joint ownership.
Under the Umbrella Final Agreement, a Yukon First Nation holds Settlement Land. All other land in Yukon is Non-Settlement Land.
Iceland has private land and national lands (þjóðlendur). On national lands, the Icelandic state owns the land and all land rights that are not private property.

Finnmarkseiendommen (the Finnmark Estate) is a separate legal body that owns the land that Statskog SF held in Finnmark. The Finnmark Act keeps the land rights that the Sami and other people have from long use.
Seven Treaty Parties claim parts of Antarctica, and other countries do not recognize these claims. Article IV of the Antarctic Treaty freezes all claims while the Treaty is in force.

fields.label: What the territory rule says about owners
codes: Under the Land Code of the Russian Federation, land can be private, municipal or state property. All land that citizens, legal entities or municipalities do not own is state property.
unknown: we did not read an official page about who owns the land.

Alaska is a mix of federal land, State of Alaska land, Alaska Native Corporation land and other private land. In 1959, when Alaska became a state, almost all of its land was federal. The BLM surveys land and transfers it to individual Alaska Natives, Alaska Native corporations and the State of Alaska.
Land in Nunavut is Crown land, Commissioner's land or Inuit Owned Land. Some privately owned land is also inside municipal boundaries.

Greenland has joint ownership of land. Thus, nobody can buy or sell land. A person or a company gets a right of use through an area allotment. The official page says joint ownership, not public land. Here, our class 'public land' means this joint ownership.
Under the Umbrella Final Agreement, a Yukon First Nation holds Settlement Land. All other land in Yukon is Non-Settlement Land.
Iceland has private land and national lands (þjóðlendur). On national lands, the Icelandic state owns the land and all land rights that are not private property.

Finnmarkseiendommen (the Finnmark Estate) is a separate legal body that owns the land that Statskog SF held in Finnmark. The Finnmark Act keeps the land rights that the Sami and other people have from long use.
Seven Treaty Parties claim parts of Antarctica, and other countries do not recognize these claims. Article IV of the Antarctic Treaty freezes all claims while the Treaty is in force.

We did not read an official page about land or research permits in northern Labrador. Find the permit authority before field work.

We did not read an official page about land or research permits in northern Saskatchewan. Find the permit authority before field work.

Ask the Expedition Office of the Government of Greenland for an expedition permit. You must have a permit for all activities in the National Park and for most stays on the Ice Sheet and in some remote areas.

The Government of Yukon site refused our requests. Thus, we did not read its licence pages. Find the permit authority before field work. On Settlement Land, the Yukon First Nation holds the rights of an owner.

All research in the Northwest Territories must have a licence or a permit. The Aurora Research Institute licenses most research. Research on fish and marine mammals also must have a licence from Fisheries and Oceans Canada.

The Outdoor Recreation Act permits all persons to walk in uncultivated land (utmark) all year. For other field work, find the landowner first. In a protected area, ask the management authority that the map names.

In a protected area in the care of Náttúruverndarstofnun, research must have a permit from Náttúruverndarstofnun before the work starts. On national lands, most use of land must have a permit from the municipality concerned.

The right of public access (allemansrätten) permits you to walk and camp in nature if you respect the landowners. In a protected area, ask the county administrative board (Länsstyrelsen) that the map names as manager.
Ask Finnmarkseiendommen (FeFo) about use of its land. In a protected area, the rules of that area apply, and the map gives its management authority.
Ask Statsforvalteren i Nordland for a dispensation from the rules of Jan Mayen naturreservat. The reserve covers the whole island except the station area and a small area in Kvalrossbukta.
Register all research in the Research in Svalbard (RiS) portal. Most field activities must have permission from Sysselmesteren på Svalbard (the Governor). The Governor manages all protected areas.
Ask the relevant national competent authority of an Antarctic Treaty Party for the necessary permits before the visit. To go into an ASPA, you must have a permit from an appropriate authority.

thermal_inertia.label: Thermal inertia

thermal_inertia.source: LRO Diviner derived data bundle, PDS (product inventories read)

rock_abundance.label: Rock abundance
rock_abundance.note: We made sure that the Diviner map of rock abundance covers only the latitudes -80 to 80 deg (label MINIMUM/MAXIMUM_LATITUDE). The centre of this lunar region is at -89.46 deg, nearer the pole than the edge of the map. Thus, Diviner gives no rock abundance here. We did not find another public map of rock abundance for the lunar poles.
rock_abundance.source: LRO Diviner Level 3 rock abundance, label dgdr_ra_avg_cyl_128_img.lbl

hydrogen.label: Near-surface hydrogen or water
hydrogen.note: The value is for the half-degree bin that holds the centre of the lunar region. The 264 bins with centres in the lunar region have values from 143.8 to 147.4 ppm. The instrument cannot tell the difference between ice in a cold trap and hydrogen that is mixed through the soil.
hydrogen.source: Lunar Prospector neutron spectrometer, 'Hydrogen_halfdeg' (Feldman et al. 2001), PDS Geosciences Node

ice_depth.label: Share of ground with ice stable within 1 m

surface_activity.label: Surface activity
surface_activity.unit: m per Earth year where a rate is given
surface_activity.note: We expect none, because there is no wind and no liquid water. New impact craters and rare slides on slopes are the only known changes. The NASA south-pole release of 2024 says that a light seismic motion can make some slopes slide. It names the inner walls of Shackleton and Nobile Rim 1.
surface_activity.source: NASA release, 25 January 2024 (Watters et al. 2024, Planetary Science Journal)

large_quakes.label: Quakes
large_quakes.text: Strong shallow moonquakes are possible in the south-polar region. There is no local count.
large_quakes.note: The strongest shallow moonquake that the Apollo seismometers recorded (1969-1977) had its epicentre in the south-polar region. Its exact place is not known. The area of possible epicentres covers many Artemis III candidate regions. Young thrust-fault scarps are near some of these regions, and in some of them. There is no published count or rate for this lunar region. No seismometer worked near the south pole at any time.
large_quakes.source: NASA release, 25 January 2024 (Watters et al. 2024, Planetary Science Journal)

rules.name: Snow-free months (used by rules 2, 4 and 6)
rules.words: The calendar months whose mean air temperature 2 m above the ground is above 0 C in the NASA POWER grid (temperature_cells.json for the Moon part, mars_climate.json for the Mars part). Where no month is above 0 C, the single warmest month. Taken from temperature, not from the snow maps, so that the Moon and Mars parts use the same rule.
rules.note: A rough estimate by our own rule. It is not a measurement.
rules.words_on_page: Where no month is above 0 C, the single warmest month. Taken from temperature, not from the snow maps, so that the Moon and Mars parts use the same rule.

rules.name: Rockiness
rules.words: high when at least 0.5 of the land is bare, the ground is steep or rough (90th-percentile slope of 10 degrees or more, or roughness at 90 m at least that of the smoothest lunar region) and the rock map does not say loose sediment; low when under 0.25 of the land is bare, or the rock map says loose sediment and the 90th-percentile slope is under 5 degrees; medium otherwise. Mars part: no 90 m roughness is held, so steep-or-rough is the slope test alone, and its slopes are taken across about 3.7 km, which reads flatter than the Moon part's 90 m slopes.
rules.note: A rough estimate by our own rule. It is not a measurement.
rules.words_on_page: low when under 0.25 of the land is bare, or the rock map says loose sediment and the 90th-percentile slope is under 5 degrees. medium otherwise.

rules.name: How fast the ground heats and cools
rules.words: index = mean of (1 - albedo) over the snow-free months divided by the mean daily temperature swing of air at 2 m over the same months (months where both are known), in 1 per degree C. The places of each output file are cut into thirds by this index: the lowest third reads 'heats and cools fast, like dry dust or sand', the middle third 'in between', the highest third 'slow, like rock or wet ground'. Both inputs come from coarse climate grids (NASA POWER: CERES 1 degree albedo, MERRA-2 air temperature swing), not from the ground at the place.
rules.note: A rough estimate by our own rule. It is not a measurement.
rules.words_on_page: Both inputs come from coarse climate grids (NASA POWER: CERES 1 degree albedo, MERRA-2 air temperature swing), not from the ground at the place.

rules.name: Mineral family
rules.stands_in_for: mineralogy, spectral match and silicate composition
rules.words: read from the rock map's class by one table (meta.mineral_family_table): basic volcanic rock gives 'basalt minerals (plagioclase, pyroxene, olivine): like the Moon's dark plains and like Mars'; a place on a listed anorthosite body (data/reference/anorthosite_bodies.json) gives 'plagioclase-rich: like the Moon's bright highlands' with the body's listed feldspar composition (An number), and this wins over the map's class; every other class gets its usual minerals in a few plain words. Ice, water and no-data boxes give null. Read from a rock map, not from spectra.
rules.note: A rough estimate by our own rule. It is not a measurement.
rules.words_on_page: every other class gets its usual minerals in a few plain words. Ice, water and no-data boxes give null. Read from a rock map, not from spectra.

rules.name: Water in the top soil
rules.words: dry, moist or wet by thirds of the mean top-soil wetness (NASA POWER GWETTOP, 0 dry to 1 saturated) over the snow-free months, cut over the places of each output file (cut values in meta.cuts); null where the model's grid point is ice (soil_wetness_ice_flag). Ground ice: likely when the mean permafrost probability is 0.5 or more, possible from 0.1 to under 0.5, unlikely under 0.1; in Antarctica likely, by the literature note of rock_frozen_cells.json (not a map value); where the map has no value, unlikely when the yearly mean air temperature is 3 C or more, else null.
rules.note: A rough estimate by our own rule. It is not a measurement.
rules.words_on_page: null where the model's grid point is ice (soil_wetness_ice_flag). Ground ice: likely when the mean permafrost probability is 0.5 or more, possible from 0.1 to under 0.5, unlikely under 0.1. in Antarctica likely, by the literature note of rock_frozen_cells.json (not a map value). where the map has no value, unlikely when the yearly mean air temperature is 3 C or more, else null.

rules.name: Depth to frozen ground
rules.words: from the permafrost zone: continuous -> shallow; discontinuous -> shallow in most of the area; sporadic -> patchy; isolated patches -> rare; none -> none expected; Antarctica -> shallow (literature); where the map has no value, none expected when the yearly mean air temperature is 3 C or more (as in rule 4), else null. Classes only, no metres: the open pages opened tonight gave no zone-by-zone rule of thumb for the thickness of the summer-thawed layer (meta.frozen_ground_depth_sources).
rules.note: A rough estimate by our own rule. It is not a measurement.

Antarctica -> shallow (literature). where the map has no value, none expected when the yearly mean air temperature is 3 C or more (as in rule 4), else null. rules.name: Sand and dust on the move
rules.words: likely where the ground is loose sediment (rock map) or mostly bare (bare share 0.5 or more), the top soil is in the dry third and the mean wind at 10 m over the snow-free months is 6 m/s or more; unlikely where the top soil is in the wet third, or the ground is frozen (the model's grid point is ice, or the rock map says ice and glaciers), or mostly not bare (bare share under 0.25: plants, ice or water); possible otherwise.
rules.note: A rough estimate by our own rule. It is not a measurement.
rules.words_on_page: possible otherwise.

rules.name: Ilmenite-bearing rock possible
rules.words: possible where the rock map says basic volcanic rock or the place lies on a listed anorthosite body (iron-titanium oxide deposits occur in both); otherwise unlikely; null where the map says ice, water or no data and no body is listed.
rules.note: A rough estimate by our own rule. It is not a measurement.
rules.words_on_page: possible where the rock map says basic volcanic rock or the place lies on a listed anorthosite body (iron-titanium oxide deposits occur in both). otherwise unlikely. null where the map says ice, water or no data and no body is listed.

rules.words: volcanic, 'steady volcanic effects likely': a volcano that erupted in 3 or more separate years since 1990, or at any time since 2015, lies within 30 km of the place's centre. What it means for the work: gas and volcanic haze that can corrode and fog instruments and optics; fine ash and abrasive dust on the ground and in the air; warm or steaming ground that upsets temperature readings; small volcanic tremors; closures of the area when it erupts.

What it means for the work: gas and volcanic haze that can corrode and fog instruments and optics; fine ash and abrasive dust on the ground and in the air; warm or steaming ground that upsets temperature readings; small volcanic tremors; closures of the area when it erupts.

rules.words_on_page: volcanic, 'none expected': otherwise.

rules.words: volcanic, 'young volcanic ground (useful side, yes or no)': yes when a Holocene volcano (active in the last ~11,700 years, any date) lies within 50 km and the rock map (data/derived/rock_frozen_cells.json or mars_rock_frozen.json, when present) calls the place's rock volcanic; no when there is no such volcano within 50 km or the rock map says the rock is not volcanic; null when a volcano is that close but the rock map gives no class. Fresh lava and ash are a good stand-in for the basalt soil of the Moon's dark plains and of Mars.

rules.words: human, 'steady human disturbance likely': a listed settlement of 1,000 or more people lies within 5 km, or a main road or railway within 2 km, or an airfield with scheduled flights within 10 km. What it means for the work: vibration from vehicles and aircraft; radio noise; dust raised by traffic; artificial light; tracks and litter in camera views.

rules.words: human, 'human disturbance possible': a listed settlement of any size lies within 25 km, or a main road or railway within 10 km, or an airfield of any kind within 10 km. What it means for the work: vibration from vehicles and aircraft; radio noise; dust raised by traffic; artificial light; tracks and litter in camera views.

rules.words: human, 'undisturbed as far as our lists show': otherwise.
rules.words_on_page: human, 'undisturbed as far as our lists show': otherwise.

rules.words: human, 'help within reach (useful side, yes or no)': yes when a listed settlement of 1,000 or more lies within 50 km or an airfield with scheduled flights within 100 km (power, shelter, rescue); no otherwise.
rules.words_on_page: no otherwise.

rules.words: small tremors, 'small tremors likely': a volcano that erupted since 1990 lies within 50 km, or at least 5 earthquakes of magnitude 5 or more were catalogued within 200 km since 1990.

small tremors, 'small tremors possible': a Holocene volcano of any date lies within 100 km, or 1 to 4 earthquakes of magnitude 5 or more within 200 km since 1990, or glacier ice covers 10% or more of the area's land (moving ice makes small quakes).
small tremors, 'small tremors unlikely': otherwise.
rules.words_on_page: small tremors, 'small tremors unlikely': otherwise.

rules.name: small tremors
rules.words: our rule of thumb, not an engineering standard: 'steady small tremors' when catalogued events fell within 100 km in at least 12 of the 16 years and at a rate of at least 5 a year; 'occasional small tremors' when at least one fell within 100 km but not steadily (in 1 to 11 of the years, or under 5 a year; 1 to 3 years is usually a single swarm); 'none recorded' when the catalogue records small tremors here and none was catalogued within 100 km; 'cannot tell' when the catalogue cannot see small tremors here, and also when it sees only tremors above some magnitude between 2.5 and 3.5 and none was catalogued within 100 km (an empty circle then says nothing about smaller ones).
rules.words_on_page: 1 to 3 years is usually a single swarm). 'none recorded' when the catalogue records small tremors here and none was catalogued within 100 km.

rules.name: can the catalogue see
rules.words: The detection floor is the 10th percentile of the magnitudes of all catalogued events from 1 to under 5 within 500 km over the 16 years (null if fewer than 30 events). 'small tremors are recorded here' when the floor is at or below 2.5; 'only tremors of magnitude M and above are recorded here' when it is above 2.5 and at most 3.5; 'small tremors cannot be seen in this catalogue here' when it is above 3.5 or there are too few events to tell. A floor at or below 2.5 counts only if the catalogue also lists at least one event under that magnitude within 200 km of the place (field floor_check); otherwise the low floor is borrowed from a better-watched network farther away, as western Alaska seen from Chukotka or Texas seen from Coahuila, and the place is read as 'cannot be seen'. Where small tremors cannot be seen the counts are null, never 0: no record is not the same as no tremors.
rules.words_on_page: 'small tremors are recorded here' when the floor is at or below 2.5. 'only tremors of magnitude M and above are recorded here' when it is above 2.5 and at most 3.5. 'small tremors cannot be seen in this catalogue here' when it is above 3.5 or there are too few events to tell. Where small tremors cannot be seen the counts are null, never 0: no record is not the same as no tremors.

rules.name: power
rules.words: Panel yield, rule of thumb: kWh a day from each kilowatt of panels = sunlight on level ground (kWh per square metre per day) x 0.75. A panel's kilowatt rating assumes 1 kW per square metre of sunlight; 0.75 allows for heat, dirt, snow, wiring and inverter losses. Panels tilted toward the Sun do better at high latitude (a low Sun hits a level panel at a glancing angle); that is not counted here.
rules.words_on_page: A panel's kilowatt rating assumes 1 kW per square metre of sunlight; 0.75 allows for heat, dirt, snow, wiring and inverter losses. Panels tilted toward the Sun do better at high latitude (a low Sun hits a level panel at a glancing angle). that is not counted here.

rules.name: power
rules.words: Solar class 'good': yearly mean sunlight on level ground of at least 4.5 kWh per square metre per day (about 1,640 kWh per square metre a year).

rules.name: power
rules.words: Solar class 'fair': from 3.0 up to 4.5 kWh per square metre per day; 'poor' below 3.0. These cut values are our own: sunny deserts (5.5 to 7) read good, central Europe (about 3) fair to poor, the high Arctic (about 2) poor.
rules.words_on_page: Solar class 'fair': from 3.0 up to 4.5 kWh per square metre per day; 'poor' below 3.0.

rules.name: power
rules.words: A month counts as having no sunlight (polar night) when NASA POWER gives exactly 0.0 for it; a month the service leaves blank is unknown (null), not dark.
rules.words_on_page: A month counts as having no sunlight (polar night) when NASA POWER gives exactly 0.0 for it. a month the service leaves blank is unknown (null), not dark.

rules.name: power
rules.words: Sunlight above the air at the distance of Earth and the Moon from the Sun: 1,361 watts per square metre (NASA NSSDCA Earth and Moon fact sheets, saved in this project). At the Moon's south pole a panel standing upright and facing a Sun on the horizon receives all of it, because there is no air.
rules.words_on_page: At the Moon's south pole a panel standing upright and facing a Sun on the horizon receives all of it, because there is no air.

rules.name: power
rules.words: Air mass at Sun height h (degrees), the thickness of air the sunlight crosses relative to a Sun overhead, by Kasten and Young (1989), Applied Optics 28(22), 4735-4738: AM = 1 / (sin h + 0.50572 x (h + 6.07995)^-1.6364). Sea level; the place's height is not counted.
rules.words_on_page: Sea level; the place's height is not counted.

rules.name: power
rules.words: Direct beam on a panel facing the Sun through clear air, by Meinel and Meinel (1976), Applied Solar Energy (Addison-Wesley), as quoted by PVEducation: beam = 1,361 x 0.7^(AM^0.678) watts per square metre. 0.7 is the share passed by one air mass of typical clear air; the exponent 0.678 allows for air that is not uniform.
rules.words_on_page: 0.7 is the share passed by one air mass of typical clear air; the exponent 0.678 allows for air that is not uniform.

rules.name: power
rules.words: The power is worked out at each lunar Sun ceiling (the limit_deg of each region in grazing_cells.json) and at half its height, because the Sun spends much of the low-Sun hours below the ceiling.

rules.name: power
rules.words: A place's clear-sky share in its best ten-day periods = mean of (1 - cloud percent / 100) over the months of the ten-day periods listed in grazing_cells.json under targets.<region>.top_bins, weighted by the low-Sun hours of each period. Cloud percent is cloud_pct of cloud_cells.json (monthly mean over all hours, CERES SYN1deg). The low-Sun power under the place's typical sky = clear-sky figure x that share. Null where the region has no best periods at the place or the cloud is unknown.
rules.words_on_page: Cloud percent is cloud_pct of cloud_cells.json (monthly mean over all hours, CERES SYN1deg). The low-Sun power under the place's typical sky = clear-sky figure x that share. Null where the region has no best periods at the place or the cloud is unknown.

rules.name: power
rules.words: Air density at sea level in the International Standard Atmosphere: 1.225 kilograms per cubic metre.
rules.words_on_page: Air density at sea level in the International Standard Atmosphere: 1.225 kilograms per cubic metre.

rules.name: power
rules.words: Air density at height z metres (International Standard Atmosphere, lower 11 km): 1.225 x (1 - 0.0065 x z / 288.15)^4.2559. z is the mean height of the model grid box the 50 m wind is given for (as the service names it in each answer); where the service gives no height, sea-level density is used and the height is null. Cold polar air is denser than the standard atmosphere (about 10 % at -15 C), which would raise the figure; that is not counted.
rules.words_on_page: Air density at height z metres (International Standard Atmosphere, lower 11 km): 1.225 x (1 - 0.0065 x z / 288.15)^4.2559. z is the mean height of the model grid box the 50 m wind is given for (as the service names it in each answer). where the service gives no height, sea-level density is used and the height is null. Cold polar air is denser than the standard atmosphere (about 10 % at -15 C), which would raise the figure; that is not counted.

rules.name: power
rules.words: Factor for the usual spread of wind speeds: if speeds follow a Rayleigh distribution the mean of the speed cubed is 6 / pi = 1.91 times the mean speed cubed, which is how the standard 50 m wind classes were tied to mean speeds.

rules.name: power
rules.words: Power in the wind at 50 m = 0.5 x air density x 1.91 x (yearly mean speed)^3, in watts per square metre of rotor area: the power the moving air carries, not what a turbine delivers (a turbine takes at most 59 %, in practice 35 to 45 %). The yearly mean speed is the plain mean of the 12 monthly means of NASA POWER's WS50M.
rules.words_on_page: The yearly mean speed is the plain mean of the 12 monthly means of NASA POWER's WS50M.

rules.name: power
rules.words: Wind power classes 1 to 7 at 50 m (US Department of Energy and NREL, Elliott et al. 1986, Wind Energy Resource Atlas of the United States; at sea level these match mean speeds of 5.6, 6.4, 7.0, 7.5, 8.0 and 8.8 m/s): class 1 below 200 W per square metre, 2 from 200, 3 from 300, 4 from 400, 5 from 500, 6 from 600, 7 from 800. The bands are from the published table as we know it; no copy was saved tonight.
